revatīvimānaṃ.meaning_2: the Revatī Mansion; the story of Revatī's mansion
revatīvimānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the second vimāna story in the Vimānavatthu; nominative singular in the text.
revatīvimānaṃ.translation_1: The Mansion Story of Revati, the Second.

khīṇāyukañca.meaning_2: with exhausted life; whose lifespan has ended; with expired life expectancy; short-lived
khīṇāyukañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form is khīṇāyukaṃ (accusative singular agreeing with maṃ) with the enclitic -ca attached. The -ka suffix is adjectival.
khīṇāyukañca.example_1: 1012. ‘‘ Khīṇāyukañca maṃ ñatvā, sarīraṃ pādāsi satthuno;
khīṇāyukañca.translation_1: Knowing that my lifespan was ending, I gave my body to the Teacher.

pañcettha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of pañca + ettha; 'ettha' refers to the place in the verse, = 'here'. Subject is nāriyo.
pañcettha.example_1: 317. Pañcettha nāriyo āgamaṃsu nhāyituṃ, sītodakaṃ uppaliniṃ sivaṃ nadiṃ;
pañcettha.translation_1: 317. Five ladies came here to bathe, in the river Sītodaka, with lotuses, a peaceful river;

ucchāgāraṃ.meaning_2: sugar-cane house; dwelling made of sugar cane
ucchāgāraṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. The first member ucchu has become ucchā before agāra.
ucchāgāraṃ.translation_1: “Whoever gives a dwelling made of sugarcane, a dwelling made of grass, or a dwelling made of cloth;

bhāgaḍḍhabhāgaṃ.meaning_2: half of the share; half of one's portion
bhāgaḍḍhabhāgaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. The PEU splits it as bhāga + aḍḍhabhāga, i.e. 'half of the share'; it could also be read as a dvanda-type bhāga + aḍḍhabhāga, 'a share and half a share'.
bhāgaḍḍhabhāgaṃ.translation_1: having given half of half, I delight in Nandana Grove.

accharāgaṇaghosito.meaning_2: resounding with the voices of groups of celestial nymphs; filled with the sound of choirs of female deities
accharāgaṇaghosito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahuvrīhi compound: 'whose sound is the host of nymphs'. Nominative singular modifying the subject of the verse. The related PEU entry's 'pleased by' is not supported by the Pāḷi; ghosita here means 'resounding with'.
accharāgaṇaghosito.translation_1: Resounding with various musical instruments, filled with the songs of celestial choristers.

idhāgatosi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of idhāgata (come here) + asi (you are). 2nd singular present of atthi with the adjective idhāgata; in the text addressed to a yakkha.
idhāgatosi.example_1: Mayampi naṃ daṭṭhukāmamha yakkha, yassānukampāya idhāgatosi;
idhāgatosi.translation_1: We too wish to see him, O yakkha, for whose compassion you have come here;

sumedhanāmassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound describing the Buddha (jinassa); genitive singular in the text. Sumedha here is the name of the 14th previous Buddha, but the compound only says 'named Sumedha'.
sumedhanāmassa.example_1: 1203. ‘‘ Ahaṃ bhadante ahuvāsi pubbe, sumedhanāmassa jinassa sāvako;
sumedhanāmassa.translation_1: “Venerable sir, I was formerly a disciple of the Victor named Sumedha;

itthivimānaṃ.meaning_2: stories of the female spirits; mansion of women; women's mansion
itthivimānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the Vimānavatthu section. Nominative singular in the text.
itthivimānaṃ.translation_2: The stories of the female spirits are finished.

malyadhare.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of mālyadhara, with the cluster ly for lly. Vocative plural in the text, agreeing with alaṅkate and suvatthe.
malyadhare.translation_1: Adorned, wearing garlands, and well-dressed, you shine like lightning in the clouds.
malyadhare.translation_2: Adorned with garlands and beautifully clothed, you shine like lightning in the clouds.

mālyadhare.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of mālādhara with the Sanskritising spelling mālya; locative singular agreeing with alaṅkate in the verse.
mālyadhare.translation_1: Adorned, wearing garlands, and well-dressed, you shine like lightning in the clouds.

suvatthe.meaning_2: well-dressed; wearing good clothes; beautifully clothed
suvatthe.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text this is locative singular, used as an adjective describing the deity. See also suvatthā.
suvatthe.translation_1: Adorned, wearing garlands, and well-dressed, you shine like lightning in the clouds.
suvatthe.translation_2: Adorned with garlands and beautifully clothed, you shine like lightning in the clouds.

vijjurivabbhakūṭaṃ.meaning_2: like lightning in the summit of a storm-cloud
vijjurivabbhakūṭaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vijju (fem) + iva + abbhakūṭaṃ; the simile 'like lightning in a cloud' describes radiant appearance. Accusative singular in the text.
vijjurivabbhakūṭaṃ.translation_1: Adorned, wearing garlands, and well-dressed, you shine like lightning in the clouds.
vijjurivabbhakūṭaṃ.translation_2: Adorned with garlands and beautifully clothed, you shine like lightning in the clouds.

abbhāgatānāsanakaṃ.meaning_2: seat for those who have arrived; seat for guests
abbhāgatānāsanakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. The compound members are abbhāgata and āsanaka; the first member is in the plural sense ("for those who have arrived").
abbhāgatānāsanakaṃ.translation_1: 5. “I, when I was a human among human beings, gave a chair to those who had arrived.

paṭhamapīṭhavimānaṃ.meaning_2: the First Pīṭha Mansion; the story of the first celestial mansion of the seat; name of a Vimānavatthu story
paṭhamapīṭhavimānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the Vimānavatthu chapter, nominative singular; pīṭha here 'seat, chair; bech', vimāna 'celestial mansion'.
paṭhamapīṭhavimānaṃ.translation_1: The First Chair Mansion, the First.
